projects.title: End-to-End Chronic Disease Prediction
projects.short_description: Reproducible machine-learning classification pipeline with data preprocessing, threshold tuning, and an interactive Streamlit risk assessment interface.
projects.overview: An end-to-end predictive healthcare machine learning project classifying individual chronic disease risk from behavioural survey data. Spanning data acquisition, cleaning, imbalance handling, model benchmarking, probability calibration, and deployment via an interactive Streamlit web dashboard.
projects.problem: Public health datasets feature substantial class imbalance, noisy self-reported indicators, and skewed distributions where default classification thresholds fail to catch high-risk individuals.
projects.solution: Built a modular pipeline handling missing values, encoding categoricals, and tuning decision thresholds to prioritize high recall on vulnerable cases without collapsing precision.
projects.personal_contribution: Independently implemented data preprocessing, exploratory statistical visualizations, class imbalance evaluation, model selection, probability threshold optimization, and Streamlit prediction interface.
limitations: Experimental classification model based on survey data (CDC BRFSS ~253k records); not a clinically validated diagnostic tool.
High recall (~91%) is achieved by shifting the decision threshold to ~0.35, resulting in trade-offs with false positive rates (precision ~37.89%).

results.value: 253,680 rows, 20 features

projects.title: Web Data Acquisition & Structured Extraction
projects.short_description: Automated web scraping pipeline extracting structured catalog data with error handling, rate limiting, and tabular data normalization.
projects.overview: A data engineering workflow designed to ingest, parse, clean, and structure catalog data from multi-page web sources into validated datasets.
projects.problem: Dynamic web pages and pagination require structured traversal, graceful error recovery on transient failures, and clean schema normalization.
projects.solution: Built automated extractors using Requests, Beautiful Soup, and Selenium with session pooling, DOM selectors, schema validation, and Pandas tabular export.

limitations: Targeted at structured public e-commerce catalogs (e.g. Books to Scrape); does not bypass complex CAPTCHA challenges.
Requires DOM selector maintenance if target markup structures change.

projects.title: Car Price Analysis & Predictive Modeling
projects.short_description: Exploratory multivariate statistical analysis, outlier treatment, and regression modeling of automotive market values.
projects.overview: A data analysis and regression modeling study examining automotive features (engine size, curb weight, horsepower, fuel system) to understand pricing mechanics and build predictive pricing models.
projects.problem: Automotive pricing data contains non-linear interactions, multi-collinearity, and extreme high-end outliers that skew baseline linear models.
projects.solution: Conducted systematic exploratory data analysis, visual correlation heatmaps, log-transformations for skewed values, and cross-validated regression models.
projects.personal_contribution: Authored complete exploratory data analysis notebooks, correlation diagnostics, feature scaling, and regression benchmark comparisons.
limitations: Based on historical dataset sample; prices do not reflect current secondary market inflation or macroeconomic currency shifts.
Regression performance is bounded by available physical specs without vehicle condition metrics.

results.value: Engine size, horsepower, and curb weight identified as top price drivers
Categorical one-hot encoding and standardized scaling pipeline

projects.title: NVIDIA Stock Volatility & Movement Prediction
projects.short_description: Comparative time-series machine-learning study evaluating 10 classification algorithms on historical hourly market features.
projects.overview: A machine-learning experiment studying market price movements and volatility of NVIDIA (NVDA) stock. Historical hourly OHLCV data was retrieved, enriched with lagged technical indicators and volatility metrics, and modeled across ten scikit-learn classifiers.
projects.problem: Financial time-series data suffers from severe non-stationarity, low signal-to-noise ratio, and temporal leakage risks when standard cross-validation is naively applied.
projects.solution: Engineered rolling z-scores, lagged returns, and volatility spreads; enforced chronologically ordered evaluation splits to prevent lookahead bias; benchmarked 10 distinct models.
projects.personal_contribution: Built data ingestion script via yfinance, feature engineering pipeline (lagged indicators, volatility metrics), model training harness across 10 classifiers, and confusion matrix analysis.
limitations: Educational and research model; past statistical predictive scores do NOT guarantee profitable trading or future returns.
Class imbalance in movement targets requires careful threshold inspection. Transaction fees and slippage were not modeled.

results.value: 2 years hourly OHLCV market records
AdaBoost Classifier
~0.7283 on experimental test split
10 algorithms (AdaBoost, XGBoost, Random Forest, SVC, etc.)

projects.title: Experimental Character-Level NLP Grammar Correction
projects.short_description: Neural text classification model using character-level hashing vectorization to detect and correct grammatical token errors.
projects.overview: An experimental natural language processing project developed within the DEPI program investigating character-level n-gram representations for high-cardinality grammatical error correction.
projects.problem: Word-level vocabularies often fail on misspelled or morphologically corrupted tokens, creating out-of-vocabulary bottlenecks in low-resource grammar checkers.
projects.solution: Employed character-level n-gram HashingVectorizer paired with a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) neural classifier (hidden layers: 512, 256, 128) predicting correction targets across approximately 6,411 token classes.
projects.personal_contribution: Implemented character-level n-gram vectorization pipeline, trained MLPClassifier neural network, conducted experimental evaluation across word-level and sentence-token metrics.
limitations: Experimental model; token-level classification accuracy is not equivalent to full human-level sentence grammatical fluency.
Preliminary owner-reported results: validation accuracy ~59.8%, word-level test accuracy ~56.8%, sentence-token accuracy ~70.3%.

results.value: ~6,411 token classes
MLP (512, 256, 128 hidden units)
70.3% (Preliminary reported)
56.8% (Preliminary reported)

projects.title: Sports Club Management System
projects.short_description: Java desktop system featuring domain modeling and a custom first-child/next-sibling Trie for prefix search.
projects.overview: A desktop management application written in Java featuring Swing GUI and domain data models (Sport, Club, Member). It is highlighted by a custom Trie data structure implementing efficient prefix search alongside dual-index lookups.
projects.problem: Prefix matching across large membership registries requires specialized index structures rather than naive linear table scans.
projects.solution: Implemented a custom Trie using a memory-efficient first-child/next-sibling representation alongside separate ID and name index tables.
projects.personal_contribution: Independently implemented custom Trie prefix tree, domain entities, Swing desktop user interface, and indexing search logic.
limitations: In-memory data store with file persistence; does not currently run on external relational database server.
Benchmarking and comprehensive invariant test suites noted in early documentation remain open for future extension.

results.value: Custom Trie with first-child/next-sibling node pointers
Dual index tables for O(1) ID lookups and fast prefix matching

projects.title: Conway's Game of Life Win32 Simulation
projects.short_description: Event-driven cellular automata engine written in C++ with double-buffered Win32 GDI rendering and boundary configuration.
projects.overview: A native desktop implementation of Conway's Game of Life in C++ utilizing the native Windows Win32 API. Emphasizes clean rendering loops, double-buffering, and configurable cellular boundary dynamics.
projects.problem: Direct GDI drawing on every tick causes heavy visual flickering and high CPU load during large-grid cellular iterations.
projects.solution: Implemented an off-screen memory device context (double buffering) for seamless rendering, bit-manipulation cell state evaluation, and configurable boundary rules (toroidal vs. bounded).
projects.personal_contribution: Authored native C++ Win32 event handling, off-screen device context double-buffering, and toroidal boundary condition calculations.
limitations: Built specifically for Windows platforms using native Win32/GDI calls; not cross-platform.
Optimized for standard desktop grid resolutions rather than massive parallelized compute shaders.

results.value: Off-screen double buffering with zero screen tearing
Configurable toroidal wrap-around and hard wall edges

projects.title: Numerical Analysis Solver with Heuristic Optimization
projects.short_description: Comparative linear system solver implementing Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterative methods with heuristic method selection.
projects.overview: A computational numerical analysis suite comparing iterative matrix methods for solving linear systems of equations (Ax = b). Evaluates convergence rates and applies heuristic criteria for choosing between Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel based on matrix properties.
projects.problem: Iterative solvers diverge or converge slowly when coefficient matrices lack diagonal dominance or when system dimensions alter resource trade-offs.
projects.solution: Implemented Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel iterative algorithms with residual monitoring, convergence checking, and a heuristic rule set that selects method parameters based on available iterations and matrix characteristics.
projects.personal_contribution: Programmed iterative Jacobi and Gauss-Seidel matrix solvers, convergence testing, iteration counters, and heuristic decision rules.
limitations: Heuristic rule selection optimizes practical convergence speed but does not formally prove mathematical optimality across arbitrary non-diagonally-dominant matrices.

results.value: Jacobi & Gauss-Seidel iterative solvers
Residual error checking and iteration limit guards
